external_entities.name: duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who uses the dispatch console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.
external_entities.notes: The text does not state how an engineer signs in.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript app used by duty engineers to access the dispatch API and receive live job status.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app and our corporate web host serves it.
processes.notes: The text does not state the console's placement, exposure, or how engineers authenticate.

processes.name: corporate web host
processes.description: The host that serves the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the dispatch console and schedule importer; it reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.notes: The API is not reachable from the internet. CORS origins and credential handling were not recorded.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: A process that pulls and parses the scheduling partner's SOAP feed and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The text does not state how the partner identifies the importer or how the importer identifies the partner. The importer uses an API token that has not been rotated since it was issued.

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: A database holding job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: The text does not state how the database is protected at rest.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder where the importer writes each document downloaded from the scheduling partner.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_stores.name: corporate file store
data_stores.description: The file store containing the schedule archive folder.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a folder on the corporate file store
data_stores.notes: The text names the file store as the location containing the schedule archive but does not state its network placement or storage protection.

data_flows.name: load console
data_flows.description: A duty engineer opens the dispatch console in a browser and obtains it from the corporate web host.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.

data_flows.name: cross-origin call
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API across origins.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The allowed CORS origins and whether credentials are allowed were not recorded.

data_flows.name: live job status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens and maintains a WebSocket to receive live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state whether the socket uses TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether the engineer's session is checked again after connection.

data_flows.name: read and write database
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads from and writes to the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order

data_flows.name: read SOAP feed
data_flows.description: The schedule importer pulls the scheduling partner's planned-work feed.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: The text does not state how the partner identifies the importer or how the importer identifies the partner.
data_flows.data_description: tomorrow's planned work in an XML document

data_flows.name: write archive
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive
data_flows.data_description: downloaded XML documents containing planned work

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls.
data_flows.notes: The API token was issued when the importer was built and has not been rotated since.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The network where duty engineers sit and the schedule importer runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company zone holding the live estate, with authority to move a crew and change the work a depot does that day.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: The zone controlled by the other company that publishes planned work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database's contents are confidential.
assumptions.basis: It holds job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and tokens or sessions associated with job orders; these are personal and commercially sensitive records.
